chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, raising it, who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Had it not been that plotting and deception are in the Fire, I would have been the most skillful in plotting against people.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about plotting and deception in relation to Hellfire?
ai.summary: In this famous hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) illustrates the principle of *al-istihlak* (extreme caution) by stating that if the punishment for *makr* (strategic plotting) and *khadi'ah* (deception) were not in Hellfire, he would have employed these tactics against people. This highlights that while cunning may be permissible in warfare or politics, the Ahl al-Bayt elevate it to a virtue by avoiding it out of piety and divine fear. The narration underscores the Shia emphasis on moral excellence (*ihsan*) even in matters where strict justice might permit cunning.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, raising it who said,
‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Had it not been that the plotting and the deception would be in the Fire, Iasws would have been the most skilful in evil planning’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim in a marfu’ manner who has said the following:
“Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) has said, ‘Had evil planning and deceit not been in the fire, I would have been extremely skillful in evil planning.’”
